findings.title: The prescribed remedy for the collision case is unreachable under the design's own delete-routing rule
findings.description: The Migration Plan states that when a personal key exists in both files with different values, `migrate-personal` "skips the move, leaves both files untouched," and that "clearing it is a separate, explicit `cf config unset <key> --project` the user can run." But the same document specifies "Delete: mirrors write — deletes from whichever project file the key's scope maps to," with `migrate-personal` as "the one exception that touches the *other* project file." For `git.integration_branch` (a personal key) that routes `unset --project` to `.context-forge.local.toml`, leaving the stale shared-file copy in place — so the `personal-config-in-shared-file` warning can never be cleared except by hand-editing TOML, which contradicts the slice's own Value statement (no ad hoc per-key gitignore/edit decisions). Verification Walkthrough step 9 asserts behavior that cannot occur as designed. The requirement left unmet is the plan's "defined migration/compat story." Fix options: have `migrate-personal` delete the redundant shared-file copy on the "already present, different value" path (the personal value already wins at read time, so nothing is at risk), or make `unset --project` remove the key from both project files for personal-scope keys, or add an explicit escape-hatch flag — but the design must name one.

findings.title: New ConsistencyChecker read path is under-specified: no exported file-read mechanism, and no failure mode for a missing/unparseable shared file
findings.description: The Detection rule must "scan the shared project file for any key whose `CONFIG_KEYS[key].scope === 'personal'" — i.e. enumerate which keys are *present in a specific file*. That capability does not exist: `readToml`/`resolveKey` are module-private in `packages/core/src/config/ConfigManager.ts` (not exported, contrary to the State Management section's claim that helpers are "reused as-is" — they are reusable only *inside* `ConfigManager`), and `ConfigManager.get()` resolves precedence and cannot answer "which keys sit in the shared file." `ConsistencyChecker` holds `config?: ConfigManager` (optional, undefined in several call paths), so the design must state either a new exported helper/`ConfigManager` accessor (e.g. a method returning a named file's present-key list) or a checker-local TOML read, and which `projectPath` it uses (note `cf check` constructs `ConfigManager` from the registered `project.projectPath`, so worktree-local copies are not covered). The failure modes section enumerates `migrate-personal`, `set`, and `cf init` writes but not this new read: it does not say what happens when the shared file is absent (likely fine — empty) versus malformed (currently `readToml` rethrows parse errors). Silently skipping the rule on parse failure would violate CLAUDE.md's no-silent-fallback rule, and propagating it would change `cf check` behavior for projects whose shared file is already corrupt. Either way, the strategy must be written down rather than left for implementation.

findings.title: MCP `config_get`/`config_set` tool description strings become factually wrong and are not in scope
findings.description: The Technical Scope lists the `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/configTools.ts` change as only "surface both project config paths." But that file's published tool descriptions — `config_get`: "Resolution order: project config → user config → built-in default" and `config_set`: `"project" writes to project-level config` — document the 3-tier order and the one-file meaning of "project," both of which this slice changes. Agent callers act on those strings, so the slice's own routing change silently invalidates them; the same accuracy concern initiative 900 already carries as a theme ("audit tool descriptions for accuracy"). Small, but a named integration point that must be added to the scope list and to Success Criteria (assert the description text reflects personal → shared → user → default and that "project" may resolve to either file).

findings.title: Slice frontmatter declares 914 as a prerequisite while the plan entry says "Dependencies: none"
findings.description: `dependencies: [914]` and the Prerequisites section are more accurate than the plan's "Dependencies: none" (the canonical personal key name comes from 914's rename), and 914 is already complete, so there is no scheduling impact. Worth a one-line reconciliation in the plan or the slice so the two documents don't disagree about this slice's gating.

findings.title: Two paragraphs restate the 916 prerequisite fix; a link would do
findings.description: The Overview/Value/Prerequisites/Migration-Plan text re-explains the `cf config set` default-scope bug that `916-slice.guide-update-branch-guard.md` already documents. The slice only needs to distinguish "scope resolution" (916, fixed) from "scope classification" (915, this slice) — one sentence plus a reference. Cutting the restatement trims the doc without losing any decision.
